subject: Renewal restructure — consolidate buckets, frontload burst lane
messages:
From: Linda Chen <linda.chen@acme-corp.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal restructure — consolidate buckets, frontload burst lane

Hi Tessa,

We're coming up on our renewal window (Feb 2028) and want to explore a simpler structure that aligns with our Q3 product launch. High level:
- Move from three annual buckets to a 2-year blended commitment (yr1 small, yr2 larger).
- We need a frontloaded burst lane for the first 90 days after our launch (estimated peak +40%).
- Procurement will want an escape hatch if usage drops below 60% of committed tokens in the first year.

Can you share proposals that include: co-terming options, a short escape hatch, and how credits would be consumed for burst? Also need a preliminary pricing anchor for budget planning.

Cc'ing procurement (procurement@acme-corp.com) for transparency.

Thanks,
Linda Chen
Sr. Manager, Platform Ops
Acme Corp
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Linda Chen <linda.chen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal restructure — consolidate buckets, frontload burst lane

Hi Linda —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely propose a 2-year blended commitment with a structured ramp and a defined burst lane. Initial thoughts:

- Proposal A (Recommended): 24-month blended commit with 40% of total alloc frontloaded into a 90-day burst pool. Burst pool draws from dedicated burst credits at a 1.5x token multiplier (protects baseline throughput).
- Escape hatch: 60% true-up window at 12 months with option to convert remainder to pay-as-you-go over the following 3 months (minimal termination fee if early exit).
- Co-terming: align to your fiscal year-end with prorated first-year credits to avoid double-billing.

I'll pull together a redline-ready amendment and include an operations playbook for how the burst lane is metered (KV cache priorities, burst throttling thresholds). Attaching a short usage export would help us size the burst — can you share last 3 months?

Next steps: If this direction works, I'll loop finance/legal and share a draft amendment + a preliminary price anchor by EOD Monday.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Renewals
Redwood Inference
From: Procurement <procurement@acme-corp.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Linda Chen <linda.chen@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal restructure — consolidate buckets, frontload burst lane

Tessa —

Procurement constraints:
- Must see explicit billing cadence and true-up mechanics (no ambiguous language).
- Need a contractual cap on the first-year effective rate if we agree to frontload credits.
- Escape hatch needs a clear definition and a cap on the termination fee (0–3% of committed ARR).

Please route the draft amendment and highlight the clauses so our reviewers can expedite. Also, we use DocuSign for execution.

Procurement Team
Acme Corp
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme renewal framing + escape-hatch approach

Team — forwarding Acme's asks (see thread below). Proposed structure I'm preparing for legal/finance:

1) 24-month blended commit: Yr1 = 40% of committed tokens, Yr2 = 60%.
2) 90-day burst lane = frontloaded pool (40% of Yr1) with explicit drawdown rules.
3) Escape hatch at month 12 if usage < 60% of cumulative committed tokens; true-up at a pre-agreed floor, option to convert remainder to PAYG with a 2% termination fee cap.
4) Billing cadence: quarterly invoicing with mid-year reconciliation.

Connor — can you confirm whether quarterly invoicing with a mid-year true-up fits our billing model and what the recognized revenue timing looks like?
Marissa/Karthik — can you confirm the commercial anchor (discount tiers) so I include an illustrative price table? I'll attach a draft amendment and the Q2 usage export when I have both.

Thanks,
Tessa
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme renewal framing + escape-hatch approach

Tessa —

Quarterly invoicing + mid-year reconciliation is fine. Notes:
- We'll propose a quarterly invoice cadence with a mid-year true-up checkpoint in month 6 (not just month 12) to reduce drift.
- Termination fee cap: finance is OK with a 2% cap on committed ARR for early exit if escape hatch triggered.
- Attached is a draft amendment skeleton (attachment: amendment-draft.pdf) and a Q2 usage extract I pulled (usage-report-q2.csv). Please review the definitions section — we need clear language on how burst credits are defined and consumed.

Connor O'Brien
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal restructure — consolidate buckets, frontload burst lane

Hi Linda / Procurement team —

Attached is the draft amendment (amendment-draft.pdf) and our Q2 usage export (usage-report-q2.csv) for sizing. Key points called out in the draft:
- 24-month blended commitment (Yr1/Yr2 split) with prorated first-year credits.
- 90-day burst lane: explicit draw rules and token multiplier for drawdown protection.
- Escape hatch: 60% threshold, 30-day remediation window, 2% termination fee cap.
- Billing: quarterly invoices with a month-6 reconciliation checkpoint.

Next steps: please review and let us know any redlines. When you're ready we'll publish a DocuSign envelope (link below) and schedule a 30-min alignment call to finalize pricing anchors.
